benefits: Turns any photo into a clean line drawing — great for sketch-style art and coloring pages.
The Enhance mode sharpens soft photos by reinforcing outlines without harsh halos.
A real Sobel operator, not a fake filter — the same math used in computer-vision research.

faqs.a: Edge detection finds places where brightness changes sharply — outlines, textures, text. It uses the Sobel operator: two 3x3 filters that measure horizontal and vertical change, combined into an edge strength per pixel. Pixels stronger than your threshold become lines.
faqs.q: How does edge detection actually work?

faqs.a: Detect draws a pure black-and-white (or inverted) edge map — a line drawing of your photo. Enhance blends those detected edges back into the original photo at your chosen strength, which visually sharpens outlines.
faqs.q: What is the difference between Detect and Enhance modes?

faqs.a: Raise the threshold. Low values (20–60) keep faint texture and noise as lines; high values (150–220) keep only the strongest outlines. The live preview updates as you drag.
faqs.q: How do I remove noisy speckles from the result?

faqs.a: Invert swaps black and white, giving white lines on a black background — the classic 'blueprint' look. In Enhance mode it blends dark lines instead of light ones.
faqs.q: What does the invert option do?

faqs.a: The preview is capped at 1400 px on the long edge for speed; the download matches that preview exactly. Very large originals are scaled down first.
faqs.q: Why is the download smaller than my original?

faqs.a: Soft, low-contrast images produce weak, broken edges. Photos with crisp lighting and clear outlines give the cleanest line drawings.
faqs.q: Which photos give the best edge maps?

edge-detection.formula:
Gx = [-1 0 +1; -2 0 +2; -1 0 +1] * gray
Gy = [-1 -2 -1;  0  0  0; +1 +2 +1] * gray
magnitude = sqrt(Gx^2 + Gy^2)
edge pixel = 255 if magnitude >= threshold, else 0
Enhance: out = original + (edge - original) x min(1, strength x (magnitude/255) x 2)
howTo: Upload a photo from your device (up to 15 MB).
Choose Detect for a pure line-drawing edge map, or Enhance to sharpen the original photo.
Drag the threshold slider until the lines look right — low for detail, high for bold outlines.
Optionally invert for white-on-black lines, or adjust the Enhance strength.
Press Download to save the result as a PNG.
keyFacts: Uses the Sobel operator — the industry-standard edge detector from computer vision — computed per pixel in your browser.
Detect mode outputs a clean black-and-white (or inverted) outline map of the photo.
Enhance mode blends detected edges back into the original image with an adjustable strength slider.
Threshold slider (0–255) controls how strong a brightness change must be to count as an edge.
Invert toggle gives white lines on black for the classic blueprint look.
The download is a lossless PNG rendered at up to 1400 px on the long edge.

limitations: Rendering is capped at 1400 px on the long edge, so huge originals are scaled down first.
Only the Sobel operator is offered — no Canny, Prewitt, or Laplacian variants.
Noisy or heavily compressed JPEGs produce speckled edge maps; denoise first for cleaner lines.
Enhance mode is an artistic sharpening effect, not a true deconvolution or AI upscaler.

edge-detection.workedExample:
You upload a 1200 x 800 px portrait and choose Detect with threshold 100.
A pixel on the jawline has Gx = 180, Gy = 60, so magnitude = sqrt(180^2 + 60^2) = 189.7 >= 100: it becomes a white line pixel.
A smooth cheek pixel with magnitude 24 stays black. The result downloads as edges-1200x800.png.
